chapter_name: Sarvnam Aur Uske Bhed Ka Upyog (Pronouns and Their Usage)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will discover the stunt doubles of grammar! Learn how Pronouns replace Nouns to make our sentences sound smooth and natural.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎭 What is Sarvnam? (The Noun's Stunt Double)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Imagine saying: 'Rahul woke up, then Rahul brushed Rahul's teeth, then Rahul ate Rahul's breakfast.' It sounds robotic! Sarvnam (Pronouns) like He, She, I, They (वह, मैं, तुम) step in to replace nouns, preventing boring repetition. 'Sarva' means all, 'Nam' means name—words used for all names!

Personal Pronouns have three players. First Person (Uttam Purush): The one speaking (मैं / I, हम / We). Second Person (Madhyam Purush): The one listening (तुम / You, आप / You with respect). Third Person (Anya Purush): The one being talked about (वह / He/She, वे / They).

When you point exactly at something ('यह मेरी किताब है' - This is my book), it is Nishchayvachak (Definite). But when you don't know exactly who or what it is ('दरवाजे पर कोई है' - Someone is at the door, or 'दाल में कुछ काला है' - Something is fishy), you use Anishchayvachak (Indefinite) pronouns like 'Koi' (Someone) or 'Kuch' (Something)!

Whenever you need to investigate, you call these pronouns! Words used to ask questions about nouns are Prashnavachak Sarvnam. Examples: 'कौन' (Who - used for people) and 'क्या' (What - used for things). Example: 'वहाँ कौन खड़ा है?' (Who is standing there?).

When the subject does an action by themselves, we use Reflexive Pronouns (Nijvachak). 'Nij' means 'own/self'. Words like 'स्वयं' (oneself), 'खुद' (self), or 'अपने आप' (by myself). Example: 'मैं अपना काम खुद करूँगा' (I will do my work myself).

fun_activity.title: 🤐 The 'No-Name' Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Try to describe your best friend to someone for a full minute WITHOUT using their actual name, your own name, or any specific nouns! You must use only Sarvnam (Pronouns) like He, She, They, Mine, His, Hers.

quick_recap: ⭐ Sarvnam (Pronouns) are words used in place of Sangya (Nouns) to make sentences sound natural.
⭐ Purushvachak Sarvnam represents the Speaker (First person), Listener (Second person), and Other (Third person).
⭐ Nishchayvachak points to a specific thing (This/That); Anishchayvachak points to unknown things (Someone/Something).
⭐ Prashnavachak is used for asking questions (Who/What).
⭐ Nijvachak refers back to the subject doing the action (Myself/Themselves).
